details: CONFIRMED by reading bin/ci and running ruff in check mode. The brief asked to name not-yet-existing tools as "the gate's step plainly without promising commands that do not exist"; the text says they "run before every commit, as the gate's step" in the present tense, which is both a promise that does not hold and ambiguous about who runs them. The sibling change wt/py-types adds mypy and ruff F (lint) only, so even after it there is no formatter step. Severity MEDIUM: a reachable case (ruff installed, every relay session loads this rule) produces large unrelated diffs and merge conflicts. Size: 10 agent minutes.
evidence: ruff format --check lib tests -> 41 files would be reformatted, 2 files already formatted
failing_case: A worker makes a 2-line fix in lib/relay_rules.py in a relay session. Its rules say "The formatter and the auto-fix step run before every commit, as the gate's step". bin/ci has no formatter step (grep finds no ruff/format/mypy in bin/ci) and the repo has no formatter config, but ruff is on the machine (~/.local/bin/ruff). The worker runs `ruff format lib/relay_rules.py` before committing: the diff grows by about 100 changed lines in that one file; 41 of 43 files in lib/ and tests/ would be reformatted, so parallel worktrees doing the same conflict on merge. Expected: the rule tells the agent what to do today (no hand formatting until the gate has the step), and does not state as present a gate step that does not exist. The same holds for "pinned and installed by the install script" (nothing pins or installs gate tools today). "auto-fix step" is also left undefined.
fix_hint: Rewrite the bullet as: "The gate will run the formatter and the linter's auto-fix (it corrects what it can by itself) before every commit; until that step exists, do not reformat files by hand." Same tense fix for the install-script line.
pass_cases: 1. rules/python.md says plainly that the gate has no formatter step yet and that until it has one, an agent does not run a formatter by hand over files (artifact line).
2. The rule still states the owner's target: once the gate's formatter and auto-fix step exist, they run before every commit (artifact line).

3. The tools line no longer reads as if an install script pins and installs them today (e.g. "will be pinned and installed by relay's install script"), without naming a command that does not exist (artifact line).
4. "auto-fix" is defined in a few words (the linter fixing what it can by itself) or dropped (artifact line).
5. The rule stays at or under ~350 words and keeps the '# Title' / '> gist' first lines (tests/test_python_rule.py still passes).
reason: tests/test_python_rule.py:44 passes, fails on old rule; rules/python.md lines 4-5, 11-12 say "to be pinned", "will run", "until that step exists, do not reformat files by hand", auto-fix defined.
findings.summary: the rule says the formatter and auto-fix 'run before every commit, as the gate's step', but no gate step formats and an agent obeying it reformats whole files
